races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Nursery Handicap (Birdcatcher Series)

runners_data.name: I Ready
runners_data.note: Won over this exact 6f Good combination on his third start, making him uniquely well-matched to today's conditions; sits naturally prominent and should track Shesthedevil in a position to challenge without expending energy fighting for a slot.
runners_data.comment: Winner two starts back, and I Ready returns on a sharp 17-day turnaround from stall 1 carrying 140 lb, with experience of today's distance and going in his favour. Our rating of 84 tops the nine-runner field, making him the one to beat despite the trainer's lean spell.

runners_data.name: Banks Of The Boyne
runners_data.note: Has placed twice at 6-7f on Good/Soft and moves here on the back of consecutive seconds; Wesley Joyce's 3lb claim is meaningful at nursery level and a prominent style suits a race where the leader may be catchable late.
runners_data.comment: Twice runner-up in his last three completed starts, Banks Of The Boyne arrives here fit on a 17-day turnaround with distance and going experience to call on, and his rating places him right among the principals — though he remains winless and will need to finally convert.

runners_data.name: Shesthedevil
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner, wearing a hood (hg:b), who won over this trip on Good ground — Patrick Magee has a live 14-day runner in the yard and she sets every tactical parameter; her chance depends entirely on how cleanly she establishes and whether she has improved enough since her one win.
runners_data.comment: Shesthedevil landed a win two starts back but has since disappointed with a sixth, and while she has run over today's trip and going before, her our rating of 75 leaves her with something to find on the bare form carrying 138 lb from stall 7.

runners_data.name: High Morals
runners_data.note: Has a flagged tendency to fade in the finish, which is a real concern in a race likely to require a sustained effort from the 2f pole; the 2nd at 8f on Good suggests stamina, but the fade flag and a step back to 6f raises questions.
runners_data.comment: High Morals ran a solid second two starts back and returns on a quick turnaround of just 16 days, with experience of today's distance and going working in his favour; the risk is that he has been winless in recent starts and must bounce back from an unplaced effort last time.

runners_data.name: Celestial Crown
runners_data.note: JP Murtagh's filly has four starts all over 5f and now steps up to 6f for the first time — the extra furlong may help a horse that has found rivals too quick, and Ben Coen's booking suggests connections believe the trip upgrade unlocks her.
runners_data.comment: Celestial Crown has experience over today's trip and going, and her second four starts back offers a platform, but she has been winless in recent starts with finishes of seventh, eighth and seventh suggesting she needs to find more to make a serious impact from draw nine off 129 lb.

runners_data.name: Away And Gone
runners_data.note: Donnacha O'Brien runner who holds a tongue-tie (hg:t) and hasn't run in 46 days; all three starts have been at 5-6f on Good/Soft and she holds up naturally, meaning she needs a strongly-run race to close ground in time.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts and ranked eighth of nine on our figures, Away And Gone faces a stiff ask here; she has run over today's trip and going before, and a 46-day break plus draw three are the best angles on offer.

runners_data.name: Howlin Wolf
runners_data.note: Three career runs all on Good ground with modest form figures of 4-7-7, and now steps up from 5f to 6f after a 44-day absence; without a confirmed pace scenario that truly tests the front-runners, a natural hold-up horse from this yard faces a steep ask.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts, with a pair of sevenths before a fourth last time out, Howlin Wolf is hard to fancy from a ranking of seventh of nine, though he has experience of today's distance and going and returns after a 44-day break with conditions at least familiar.

runners_data.name: Alrashdeyah
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy booked for a filly who fades late and whose natural style is deep hold-up — she is mapped to midfield here because the field is saturated with closers and she is unlikely to find a truly detached position; the fade flag combined with the style displacement makes this a difficult profile to fancy.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Alrashdeyah faces a stiff task here; she has run over today's distance and going before, and 44 days between runs suggests she returns fresh from stall four carrying 122 lb.

runners_data.name: Mr Montauk
runners_data.note: Joseph O'Brien's team has been in sharp form (T14: 6/50) and Declan McDonogh is an excellent booking, but this horse's natural style is hold-up and he has been pushed into a midfield slot by weight of numbers — his best two career efforts (2nd, 3rd) came when leading, suggesting his redistribution here undermines the very profile that has produced his placed efforts.
runners_data.comment: Consistent placed efforts mark Mr Montauk out as a genuine threat here — third two starts back and a runner-up last time out, returning on a snappy 11-day turnaround having run over today's trip and going before, with our rating of 77 suggesting he's well ahead of his official mark; the risk is he remains yet to win in recent starts.

races.paceDynamic: Shesthedevil is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival pressing for the lead, she should stride into a comfortable, uncontested gallop from the front on Good ground over 6f at the Curragh. I Ready and Banks Of The Boyne will track closely in the prominent positions just behind, creating a compact two-to-three length gap to the hold-up cluster of Celestial Crown, Away And Gone, Howlin Wolf, Alrashdeyah, and Mr Montauk. The field holds more hold-up types than the map can accommodate — Alrashdeyah and Mr Montauk are genuine deep closers redistributed to midfield, meaning they are unlikely to get their true back-of-the-field position in a 9-runner race and may end up racing closer than ideal. A sustainable, single-pace front-running scenario on a flat track in Good conditions predominantly favours prominent racers who can track the leader in a rhythm and kick in the closing stages, making the P-style horses the most structurally advantaged profile in this race shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Shesthedevil Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Shesthedevil secures a clean lead and dictates a genuine but sustainable pace with no rival pressing her.
scenarios.body: Shesthedevil dictates from the front without pressure, meaning the race is run at an honest but not brutal tempo that keeps her reserves intact into the final furlong; prominent horses who travel smoothly behind her — particularly I Ready and Banks Of The Boyne — are ideally placed to mount the only serious challenge as the leader's advantage compresses.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Overrun Leader
scenarios.trigger: If I Ready or Banks Of The Boyne move up to challenge Shesthedevil turning in, lifting the tempo and creating a strongly-run final quarter.
scenarios.body: The pace quickens sharply from the 2f pole as prominent horses commit, burning off the front-runner and turning this into a test of staying power under a pressured finish; horses with solid 6f form on Good ground who can sustain their effort are rewarded here, with I Ready's recent win at 6f on Good ground a clear asset.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Sweep Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is truly honest and the front two or three tie each other up, leaving genuine ground-covering closers to benefit in the final 100 yards.
scenarios.body: Away And Gone, Howlin Wolf, or Celestial Crown need a clear, uneventful passage from off the pace to close in time, which is structurally possible but dependent on the leaders genuinely emptying; Alrashdeyah and Mr Montauk, though redistibuted into midfield, are not guaranteed to be far enough back to produce a true sustained late run, limiting the pool of likely beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Chaos At Narrow Draw
scenarios.trigger: If the early stages produce crowding, checking, or positional shuffling that scrambles the projected running order entirely.
scenarios.body: With nine runners over 6f on a flat track, a messy break or early interference could force horses to race in completely uncharacteristic positions, nullifying pace-shape advantage entirely; this scenario disproportionately helps flexible mid-division horses who can adapt, and punishes the front-runner if she loses her rhythm.

watchPoints.text: Shesthedevil's hood (hg:b) is new headgear context — if she dwells at the break or gets caught in traffic in a 9-runner field, the entire pace map collapses and the race loses its single controlling influence.

I Ready and Banks Of The Boyne may compete aggressively for the same prominent position just off the leader — if both push forward simultaneously, the pace lifts earlier than Shesthedevil would want, turning a comfortable lead scenario into a truly pressured race.

Away And Gone (46 days) and Howlin Wolf (44 days) both return after significant breaks — watch the market moves for each; if either is sharply supported they may be set for a return to form that defies the conservative form figures.

Celestial Crown steps up in trip for the first time today (5f to 6f across all four runs) — if the extra furlong suits her, Ben Coen is capable of producing a hold-up horse late in a race with a clear lead horse to aim at.

Mr Montauk's two best career runs were placed efforts — a 2nd and a 3rd — that came when he got a more forward position than his style tag suggests; watch whether McDonogh chooses to ride him handily rather than hold up, which would contradict the pace map but could be the trainer's intention.

races.name: Irish EBF Median Sires Series Maiden
Melbourne Cup Carnival Handicap

runners_data.name: Bundle Of Interest
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer for McCreery who has finished 4th twice at 8f on good; visor fitted, 9 days fresh, and Dylan Browne McMonagle is a key booking — needs a clear run from the rear in a race where that space will be congested.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Bundle Of Interest arrives on the back of a seventh just nine days ago, though she has run over today's trip and going before and our rating has her clear of a 16-runner field, making her the one to side with.

runners_data.name: Neo Smart
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed pace-setter for Bolger; has raced prominently over 8f on good multiple times and, uncontested here, can dictate sectionals entirely to his own liking — a trainer in flat form (0/5 last 14 days) tempers the angle slightly.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, Neo Smart nevertheless shaped with promise on her latest outing nine days ago and has experience of today's distance and going; the worry is her recent sequence suggests finding one too good.

runners_data.name: Kitty Bear
runners_data.note: Won over 8f on good for Slattery and Tynan (7lb claimer) and drops to a career-low OR=65; 19 days since last run, no headgear flag, but a hold-up style means she needs pace to run into and will be caught in traffic with so many rivals sharing her preference.|
runners_data.comment: Kitty Bear has run over today's trip and going, and her win in her last six starts shows she can find the line, but four unplaced or mid-field finishes in that sequence temper expectations; 135 lb from stall 15 adds further questions for this lightly tested filly.

runners_data.name: Tofino
runners_data.note: Carroll on a hold-up type for Cromwell who was second at 8f on soft and has solid good-ground form; 33 days off and shaped well over 10f previously suggesting the mile is not a concern — a genuine each-way type if he gets a clear lane.|
runners_data.comment: Tofino has experience of today's trip and going, and our rating of 74 ranks her second of 16 — a strong case for her being the chief threat to the top-rated runner; the concern is she was second three starts back but has since gone unplaced and sixth, leaving her yet to win in her last five starts.

runners_data.name: Marambo
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for Timmons at OR=63 on a course where he has limited good-ground form (1 run in similar conditions); sits naturally just off the pace and is one of very few in this field able to track Neo Smart without overextending — that tactical position is the key asset here.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and ranked 12 of 16 on our figures, Marambo is hard to fancy, though he has run over today's distance and going before and returns after a 33-day break with experience in his favour.

runners_data.name: Comfort Line
runners_data.note: Veteran of nine seasons with two wins at 8f including on good; naturally a hold-up horse forced into a midfield berth by the crowded rear, so his best tactical option is slightly compromised, though his course familiarity and STYLE_FIT flag (0.93) both warrant caution about his quoted chance.|
runners_data.comment: Comfort Line has experience of today's trip and conditions and won five starts back, following that up with a second four starts back, but fourth last time out and a fair bit to find on official figures carrying 132 lb from stall 12.

runners_data.name: Pallatine Hills
runners_data.note: A true hold-up type for the Hartys over 8f; the redistribution here reflects that his natural finishing position is unavailable to him in this shape — his best finish on good at the trip was 5th and the STYLE_FIT discount applies.|
runners_data.comment: Pallatine Hills has run over today's trip and going, and with our rating of 74 putting him well clear of his official mark, he looks significantly thrown in on paper; the risk is that he has been winless in his last five starts, suggesting he may find a way to disappoint again.

runners_data.name: Sherekiya
runners_data.note: Unclassified runner (style=U) for Weld, three-year-old at OR=68 who placed at 8f on Heav; Chris Hayes retains the ride and Weld's training angle is always live — the unknown style gives Hayes the flexibility to slot in wherever the shape allows.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts, Sherekiya nevertheless showed a degree of improvement when fourth two runs back, and she has experience of today's trip and conditions; carrying 132 lb from stall 13 on a mark of 68, she holds some claims without being certain to improve further.

runners_data.name: Lamberella
runners_data.note: Three-year-old hold-up type for Marnane tagged with a fade-in-finish warning; was 5th over 7f on good and shaped as though the mile could stretch stamina, making the late-race fade flag particularly relevant here.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Lamberella at least has experience of today's trip and conditions to call upon, and 36 days off may have freshened her; carrying 131 lb from stall three, however, she faces a stiff task off a mark of 67 against stronger rivals.

runners_data.name: Dinamine
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old hold-up specialist (hg:p — has run in a hood) for Mulvany who boasts two wins from 12 good-ground runs at the mile; Joyce's 3lb claim helps at the weights, but the redistribution leaves him at the back of a crowded pack — best days in this configuration may be behind him.|
runners_data.comment: Dinamine ranks fifteenth of sixteen on our figures and carries a hefty 129 lb from stall 16, making him hard to fancy despite a win two starts back; he has run over today's trip and going before, but a seventh last time out does little to inspire confidence.

runners_data.name: Avec Grand Plaisir
runners_data.note: Three-year-old hold-up runner for Fahey who placed at 8f on good; shortest in the field at OR=64 but lightly raced and capable of improvement — trip looks fine but needs a gap that may not materialise.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Avec Grand Plaisir does at least bring experience of today's trip and conditions, and a third two runs back shows he can threaten the places; however, ranked eleventh of sixteen on our ratings, he faces a stiff ask from 128 lb.

runners_data.name: Sancerre Rock
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse for trainer-jockey Slattery combination, dropped into a midfield slot by the redistribution; 65 days since last run is a significant freshness concern, and the 0/4 record on good ground adds to the risk — the STYLE_FIT tag (0.90) makes this one of the more structurally compromised runners.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and ranked 13 of 16 on our figures, Sancerre Rock faces a stiff ask here; a ninth last time out does little to inspire confidence, though he has run over today's distance and going before and returns after 65 days freshened up.

runners_data.name: Ella's Gold
runners_data.note: Three-year-old with an excellent placed record (three seconds) who wears a hood (hg:p); Colgan rides and the 47-day absence is worth noting — she is a natural hold-up performer in a race that has no room for another one at the rear, and the STYLE_FIT flag (0.93) reflects the mismatch.|
runners_data.comment: Placed four times in her last five starts, Ella's Gold has solid each-way claims but remains winless in recent starts; she has experience of today's trip and going, carries 126 lb from stall one, and 47 days between runs is worth noting.

runners_data.name: Navajo Point
runners_data.note: Tagged with both a fade-in-finish warning and redistribution; raced from the back over 8f on good twice without threatening and the 1-day turnaround from last run is an unusual freshness flag — structurally one of the weakest profiles in the field.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and returning just one day after his most recent outing, Navajo Point faces a fitness query despite a second last time out; he has run over today's distance and going, and our rating of 66 offers some encouragement, but the turnaround is tight.

runners_data.name: Alto Sax
runners_data.note: Five-year-old for Peter Fahey who has won at 10f on good and placed at 9f; the redistribution from true hold-up into midfield compresses his run, but the drop to 8f may be sharper than ideal given his best form has come over further.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked 14 of 16 on our figures, Alto Sax makes little appeal under 122 lb, and two of his last four starts have yielded a fifth and a ninth, though a runner-up finish two starts back shows he retains some ability, and he has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Cannonball Queen
runners_data.note: Lowest-rated runner in the field (OR=46) with a fade-in-finish flag and a string of mid-to-back-field finishes on good; the redistribution into midfield does nothing to improve a profile that has produced four finishes of 12th or worse from five recent starts.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked last on our figures, Cannonball Queen is hard to fancy at the weights, though she has run over today's distance and going before and a return to form ten days ago — a fourth — offers a sliver of encouragement.

races.paceDynamic: Neo Smart is the one confirmed front-runner and, with no meaningful challenger for the lead, Declan McDonogh can dictate an unhurried, sustainable gallop around the Curragh mile on good ground — the classic scenario for a well-rated front-runner to control sectionals and resist. The remainder of the field is overwhelmingly hold-up in style, with Bundle Of Interest, Kitty Bear, Tofino, Lamberella, Comfort Line, Dinamine, Avec Grand Plaisir and others all wanting to race in the last half of the field, meaning Neo Smart faces no pressure whatsoever in the early stages. The field holds significantly more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate at the rear — Sancerre Rock, Pallatine Hills, Ella's Gold, Comfort Line, Dinamine, Navajo Point, Alto Sax and Cannonball Queen are all genuine back-of-the-field horses who will be shuffling for position in midfield, diluting the effectiveness of any late run. This race shape strongly favours a prominent or pace-tracking profile: a solo, uncontested leader on good ground over a true mile at the Curragh with a wall of closers behind it creates the optimal environment for a horse that can press or track Neo Smart and produce a clean, sustained finish.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Resist
scenarios.trigger: If Neo Smart dictates unchallenged from the front and the large hold-up contingent fails to produce a coordinated challenge.
scenarios.body: Neo Smart sets a comfortable, metronomic pace that denies the closers a true finishing burst, and any horse tracking within two lengths of the leader is ideally placed to capitalise if Neo Smart tires late; on good ground over a fair mile this is the textbook Curragh setup for a pace-dependent shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Tracker Picks Up Lead
scenarios.trigger: If a prominent or close-tracking horse — Marambo or Sherekiya — settles just off Neo Smart and swoops as the pace-setter flattens out in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: The race unfolds at a steady tempo with one or two horses sitting just off the leader in a pocket, and the winner peels off the pace in the straight with enough reserves to see out the distance on good ground; this profile benefits horses who can travel kindly and quicken over the last two furlongs.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Cut Through Late
scenarios.trigger: If Neo Smart goes too slow early, bunching the field, and a genuine late burst through a compressed mid-pack is triggered in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: A slow tempo paradoxically creates traffic and shuffling among the mass of hold-up horses, but the rare true finisher who finds a clear run — Tofino or Bundle Of Interest — can sustain a run all the way to the line; however, the sheer number of redistributed hold-up types crowding the same ground makes a clean passage uncertain.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough that Neo Smart cracks in the final 100 yards and a deep hold-up horse catches the entire field flat-footed.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires conditions that are not suggested by the pace map — a lone front-runner without rivals is unlikely to post a pace strong enough to set up a true late swooper — and most of the horses who would benefit are redistributed types whose natural style is compromised by the crowded rear of the field; Dinamine and Ella's Gold have the form profile but face a structural disadvantage.

watchPoints.text: Neo Smart (Declan McDonogh) — if he is allowed to bowl along unchallenged through the first three furlongs at a crawl, the entire field collapses onto his quarters and the closing sectional becomes chaotic; watch whether anyone moves to put him under early pressure.

Sherekiya (Chris Hayes / Weld) — the unknown style classification means Hayes can position this three-year-old anywhere; if Weld sends her forward to track Neo Smart, she immediately becomes one of the most dangerous horses in the race.

Traffic congestion in the straight — with eight or more hold-up and redistributed types all seeking clear running between the two-furlong pole and the line, watch for horses switching wide late, particularly Tofino (Carroll) and Bundle Of Interest (Browne McMonagle).
Navajo Point — the 1-day turnaround between runs is highly unusual for a handicapper; watch for any market move that might suggest connections have a specific reason for the quick reappearance.
Sancerre Rock — 65 days off the track, no good-ground win in four starts, and a redistribution that leaves this hold-up type structurally compromised; a drift in the market would confirm the concern.

races.name: Velo 'Official Coffee At The Curragh' Irish EBF Maiden
Tote Guarantee, Never Beaten By SP Handicap

runners_data.name: Sonoran
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator for G M Lyons who has 36 days between runs; best form came over 10f on good ground and the step back to 10f here suits, though a habit of finishing mid-pack (two placed efforts from five in similar going) raises questions about his killer instinct late.
runners_data.comment: Ranked top of the field on our rating, Sonoran arrives fresh on 36 days' rest and has run over today's trip and going, offering genuine each-way claims from stall one — though winless in his last five starts, and his last two efforts both finishing ninth, the upturn needs to come sharply.

runners_data.name: Thyer
runners_data.note: Versatile closer with the most course experience in the field; has two wins and six places at 12f on good ground previously, making this trip a tick, though a 0-from-11 strike rate on good suggests he places more than he wins.
runners_data.comment: Thyer has run over today's trip and going, and shaped with encouragement when third last time out after a testing spell; back within a fortnight and carrying 136 lb from stall six, his profile looks stronger than his official mark of 76 suggests, making him an appealing each-way proposition despite being winless in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Youcansaythatagain
runners_data.note: Three-year-old who won on debut over 10f on good here for A Oliver — a strong positive — and Ben Coen retains the ride; naturally prominent, he needs a clean position early and could be the chief danger if he avoids the prominent traffic battle.
runners_data.comment: Inconsistency is the concern here — a winner last time out but a seventh the start before that, and a rating of 71 ranked tenth of twelve suggests he has plenty to find on these terms despite the recent form boost.

runners_data.name: Great Mover
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for McCreery who finished second over 9f on soft last time; has no wins on good ground over this trip from eight attempts, and contesting the lead against Admiral Will Brown for 1m2f risks burning his stamina reserves before the straight arrives.
runners_data.comment: Placed twice in her last six starts, including a second three runs back and a third four runs back, Great Mover has experience of today's trip and going and our rating of 88 makes her a leading threat — though the unplaced run last time is the obvious concern.

runners_data.name: Unterberg
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old who won over 12f at Sligo and carries Oisin Murphy, a clear jockey upgrade; recent form over 10f on good has been poor (8th, 8th, 14th), and Laura Hourigan's 14-day figures (0 from 2) offer little encouragement despite the class of rider.
runners_data.comment: Unterberg has run over today's trip and going, and his two wins in his last six starts show he can find the winner's enclosure, though three subsequent starts have yielded little, including two eighths and an unplaced run last time out 15 days ago; the 133 lb burden is another obstacle to overcome from stall four.

runners_data.name: Admiral Will Brown
runners_data.note: Front-running three-year-old who landed a 10f win on good at the Curragh — course and going form is a genuine asset; Wesley Joyce takes the claim off the top, and if he can repel Great Mover early enough to control fractions he becomes dangerous, but a contested lead over this trip is his risk.
runners_data.comment: Won two starts back but has disappointed either side of that victory, finishing seventh on three of his last five starts, so consistency is the real question mark; has run over today's trip and going, carries 131 lb from stall two, and 20 days since his last run leaves him reasonably fresh.

runners_data.name: Liberation Date
runners_data.note: Prominently-styled filly for Jack Foley who has been running exclusively over shorter trips (8-9f); the step up to 10f is unproven, and her 0-from-five record in similar going makes her hard to trust despite the claim of apprentice Orla Tynan.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Liberation Date does bring distance and going experience to the table, and her third two runs back hints at better, but the 131 lb burden from stall 12 makes progression a tougher ask here.

runners_data.name: Mighty Danu
runners_data.note: Hold-up three-year-old for Gavin Cromwell who won a 7f maiden on good; the step up in trip and class is significant, yet Cromwell's 14-day record (3/20) shows stable form and the horse's four starts all came on good ground, making the going no concern — experience is the worry.
runners_data.comment: Mighty Danu showed she can win at this level with a victory four starts back, and her going experience is a solid foundation, but she has to prove she can recapture that form after three below-par efforts since, with 130 lb to shoulder from stall nine.

runners_data.name: Storzando
runners_data.note: Style is unconfirmed (U-rated), which adds uncertainty to how Declan McDonogh will ride him; three runs on good over 7-10f showing no win, trained by Mulvany who is 0-from-14 in the 14-day window — the horse needs to stamp a genuine identity in this race before he can be taken seriously.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts and ranked last on our figures, Storzando faces a stiff task here, though a third two starts back and experience over today's trip and going offer slim crumbs of comfort; the weight of 130 lb does him no favours either.

runners_data.name: Blackjack Hills
runners_data.note: Wears a hood and has two wins from 11 starts on good ground, both over shorter trips; the 12f attempts (8th on soft, 8th on good) raise stamina doubts, though dropping back to 10f suits better — Robbie Colgan must keep him settled if the hold-up role is to yield anything late.
runners_data.comment: Showed a turn of foot with back-to-back wins in recent starts, but has since posted an eighth and a seventh, suggesting inconsistency; he has run over today's trip and going before, and 17 days between runs keeps him fresh enough to creep back into the argument from stall three.

runners_data.name: Guinelot
runners_data.note: Won a 10f maiden on good on debut for K J Condon and Shane Foley retains the ride — a positive combination; wears a hood and has placed over 12f since, suggesting stamina is adequate, but moving from maidens to handicap company on just three runs brings a significant unknown.
runners_data.comment: Guinelot won last time out and has run over today's trip and going, which counts for something, but ranked ninth of twelve on our figures she faces a stiff task at 124 lb from stall ten.

runners_data.name: Nibras Rainbow
runners_data.note: Six-year-old who ran just four days ago and has a busy recent campaign; wears a hood, has two wins at 9-10f on good, and Chris Hayes knows the horse well — but the quick turnaround and a prominent style in a congested race could leave him vulnerable to rivals with fresher legs.
runners_data.comment: Beaten a long way back in ninth last time out and ranked 11th of 12 on our figures, Nibras Rainbow is hard to fancy despite a third and two wins in earlier recent starts; a struggling trainer — winless in 21 attempts over the last 14 days — only adds to the concern, though he has distance and going experience to call on.

races.paceDynamic: Admiral Will Brown and Great Mover are confirmed front-runners who will contest the lead from the gate over this 1m2f trip, creating an honest, competitive gallop from the outset on good ground at the Curragh. Five of the twelve runners — including Youcansaythatagain, Unterberg, Liberation Date, Guinelot, and Nibras Rainbow — want prominent positions, meaning there will be significant jostling for spots two to four furlongs in, with traffic dangers materialising around the 2-3 furlong marker as the field compresses on the straight. The dual front-runner dynamic means neither Admiral Will Brown nor Great Mover is likely to get a free lead, keeping sectionals honest throughout and burning off prominently-placed horses who can't quite get their favoured berth. This race shape — honest pace, traffic midrace, a tiring prominent pack — strongly favours genuine hold-up horses who can settle off the pace, save ground, and produce a sustained late run into a clear run.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If Admiral Will Brown and Great Mover set a genuinely contested gallop that strings out the prominent pack, leaving hold-up horses with clear daylight turning in.
scenarios.body: The dual front-runner battle burns through the early leaders and the crowded prominent group, leaving the back-runners with a flattened field to pick through in the final two furlongs; genuine closers who have settled well are ideally positioned to swoop.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Lands It
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is honest but not truly punishing and one of the prominent racers gets an uncontested berth just off the front pair with a clean passage.
scenarios.body: A horse who settles just off the pace in a ground-saving position avoids the traffic battle while still travelling within range, producing enough turn-of-foot to wear down the weakening front-runners; the Curragh straight suits those who idle into gear from close range.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Hangs On
scenarios.trigger: If one of the two lead horses — most likely Admiral Will Brown given his Curragh win profile — dominates the other early and is gifted a solo lead at a manageable tempo.
scenarios.body: With the front-runner able to dictate every split unchallenged after dropping Great Mover by halfway, the field is chasing a moving target and the straight arrives before closers wind up fully; a lone leader in fair form can exploit a modest winning time.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Mover Springs Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If the race fractures chaotically through the prominent congestion and a horse who has settled in midfield finds an unusually clean passage on the inner or outer two furlongs out.
scenarios.body: Storzando or Blackjack Hills, having avoided early scrimmaging entirely, arrives with fresh reserves as the prominent group runs themselves into the ground; this scenario requires both pace chaos and a perfectly timed split from their jockey.

watchPoints.text: Admiral Will Brown and Great Mover will fight for the lead from the start — watch whether either horse is pressured into a suicidal early fractions or one drops away by the halfway mark, as the survivor shapes the entire race.

The five prominent runners (Youcansaythatagain, Unterberg, Liberation Date, Guinelot, Nibras Rainbow) create a congestion flash-point 2-3 furlongs out — any hold-up horse on the inner risks being pocketed at the critical moment.

Nibras Rainbow ran just four days ago; watch his early movement for signs of residual fatigue — if he labours to hold his prominent position, he could drift back into the hold-up pack and cause interference.

Unterberg with Oisin Murphy is a notable jockey upgrade, but his last three good-ground runs were all poor — watch whether Murphy attempts to position him forward of his recent map or reverts to a restrained ride.

Guinelot's hood and single maiden win make him a profile that can improve sharply in handicap company — watch how Shane Foley positions him in the first half-mile as an indicator of whether the yard expects a big run.

races.name: Newbridge Silverware Royal Whip Stakes (Group 3)

runners_data.name: Cowardofthecounty
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator for Joseph O'Brien who needs a searching gallop to land a blow; OR 100 is workable in this grade but the controlled pace Charles Fort is likely to set is not ideal for a horse who wants rivals to come back to him, though course form on good going (wins at similar trips) keeps him honest at the back of this small field.
runners_data.comment: Cowardofthecounty showed genuine quality when winning four starts back, and a second two starts back underlines his consistency at this level; he has run over today's trip and going, returns fit on just ten days' rest, and his 105 rating suggests he has more to offer — though fifth last time out is the obvious concern.

runners_data.name: Omni Man
runners_data.note: Joseph O'Brien's second string carries strong trainer form (6/50 in 14 days) but his natural inclination to race prominently is compromised here — with Charles Fort already committed to the lead and A Boy Named Susie and Rebel Ascendant also wanting the front rank, he is squeezed into a midfield berth that does not play to his strengths, tempering confidence in his chance.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Omni Man nonetheless brings distance and going experience to the table, and at 135 lb from stall four he arrives fit off a ten-day turnaround with a rating of 105 suggesting he's in the mix; the worry is that he remains without a win.

runners_data.name: A Boy Named Susie
runners_data.note: Donnacha/Aidan O'Brien-trained three-year-old ridden by Oisin Murphy, a formidable combination, and his consistent recent form (five consecutive placings) suggests he handles good ground and 1m2f with ease; a 43-day absence is the only minor query, but a horse placed at this level repeatedly will likely slot into a prominent position that perfectly suits the likely race shape.
runners_data.comment: Consistently placed in recent starts, A Boy Named Susie arrives here with distance and going experience under his belt, carrying 128 lb from stall two; yet to score, but second last time out and third three starts back, he rates the one to beat on these terms.

runners_data.name: Charles Fort
runners_data.note: A P O'Brien's lightly raced three-year-old returns after a 328-day absence — the significant layoff is the headline flag — but he is the clear front-runner in this field and Wayne Lordan will be able to control the pace entirely; his sprint pedigree and early form were over shorter trips, and whether he truly stays 1m2f at Group 3 level is an open question.
runners_data.comment: Landed a win two starts back and has placed experience over today's going, with a rating of 92 supporting his claims from stall one carrying 128 lb; the significant concern is 328 days off the track, leaving his fitness very much on trust.

runners_data.name: Rebel Ascendant
runners_data.note: Jack Davison's highly rated three-year-old (OR 120, top-rated here) has run only twice, winning impressively on soft before a creditable fourth on good — that rapid rise through the ratings and a 97-day absence make him difficult to assess with confidence; races prominently and wears a hood (hg:p), and if that form is taken at face value his class should see him competitive in a race shape that suits his front-rank style.
runners_data.comment: Rated lowest in the field and returning from a 97-day absence, Rebel Ascendant is hard to fancy despite a win two starts back; he has run over today's trip and going before, and 128 lb from stall five are the neutral facts to set against a significant ratings deficit.

races.paceDynamic: Charles Fort is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with only five runners, he will dictate a controlled, honest pace from the front without any rival likely to press him for supremacy — Wayne Lordan can dictate terms at a tempo that suits his mount. The field holds more prominent types than can all secure their preferred position: Omni Man and A Boy Named Susie both want to race prominently, yet with Charles Fort already occupying the front, at least one of them will be shuffled wider or slightly further back than ideal, with Rebel Ascendant and Omni Man the likeliest to cede ground given Charles Fort's uncontested lead. A sustainable, measured pace on good ground over 1m2f at the Curragh points firmly towards horses with a prominent-to-midfield cruising position who can quicken off a true but unhurried gallop — patient hold-up horses who need a strong end-to-end pace to produce a late flourish are less favoured here.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Charles Fort dictates a fair but uncontested gallop and the race is won by a horse who travels in the first two or three throughout.
scenarios.body: Charles Fort's lone front-running role means the pace is honest but never brutal, allowing prominent trackers to conserve energy and quicken off the final bend; A Boy Named Susie and Rebel Ascendant, both travelling prominently and boasting the highest ratings in the field, are ideally positioned to pounce.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Charles Fort steals a decisive advantage at a deceptively quick early clip and the modest field never fully closes the gap.
scenarios.body: With only five runners and no challenger prepared to commit to Charles Fort early, Lordan could find himself with a comfortable cushion turning for home on quick good ground; Charles Fort's recent layoff (328 days) is a concern but A P O'Brien returns horses fit, and at OR 89 he sets a relatively low bar to clear on these terms.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Finisher Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Charles Fort goes too hard early and the race falls apart, allowing a hold-up horse to swoop from the back.
scenarios.body: Cowardofthecounty is the only true hold-up runner in the field and would need Charles Fort to uncharacteristically set a scorching pace that burns off his rivals before the home turn; on good ground over 1m2f with a field this small, that extreme scenario is unlikely, but Cowardofthecounty's winning form at this course and trip in similar conditions keeps it a live outsider possibility.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Messy Pace, Midfield Wins
scenarios.trigger: If prominent horses jostle for position behind Charles Fort and the race becomes uneven, producing a muddling gallop that flattens the field.
scenarios.body: Omni Man, racing out of his natural prominent role and mapped to midfield, could benefit if the pace becomes stop-start and his tactical versatility comes into play; this scenario requires a cluster of positional errors from the principals and is the least likely given the clarity of Charles Fort's pace-setting role.

watchPoints.text: Charles Fort's 328-day absence is the single biggest race-day risk — if he shows any signs of greenness or lack of fitness in the parade ring or early in the race, the controlled pace scenario collapses entirely.

Rebel Ascendant has run only twice and carries a hood — watch for him to get lit up in a small, competitive field and either challenge Charles Fort for the lead or miss the break, either of which reshapes the pace map.

Omni Man and A Boy Named Susie both want prominent positions; if they both push forward aggressively from the off to track Charles Fort, the pace could increase significantly above what a lone front-runner typically generates, benefiting Cowardofthecounty's hold-up profile.

Good ground is confirmed for the 4:25 at Curragh and the pace report shows consistency across all distances throughout the card — no ground deterioration expected, so all runners should encounter the conditions their form is built on.

With only five runners, any significant early position battle will be immediately visible — if Charles Fort is challenged going to the first bend rather than allowed to bowl along uncontested, revisit the front-runner-holds-on scenario upward in probability.

races.name: William Hill Irish EBF Juvenile Sprint Stakes (Listed)

runners_data.name: Grayrobin
runners_data.note: Back-to-back 5f wins at the Curragh on Good going for Kate McGivern gives her a strong course-and-conditions profile; a natural prominent runner who should secure a position just off Armor Supreme, and 23 days between runs is a comfortable freshener.
runners_data.comment: Grayrobin arrives on the back of back-to-back wins, with that sole blip an eighth three starts back, and his experience over today's trip and going is a useful asset; the chief concern is whether 131 lb blunts his momentum.

runners_data.name: Star Prospect
runners_data.note: Dylan Browne McMonagle takes over for Joseph O'Brien, adding significant jockey quality; has placed four times in five similar-going runs but hasn't won on Good, and dropping from 6f back to 5f at the Curragh is a key positive given his best effort came over the trip.
runners_data.comment: Third two starts back hints at residual ability, and Star Prospect's experience over today's trip and going stands him in good stead off 131 lb from stall five; our rating of 110 marks him as the one to beat, though last time's seventh will need reversing.

runners_data.name: April Mist
runners_data.note: Won over 5f at the Curragh on Good in just her second start for G M Lyons and Carroll; though a natural prominent type, she has been pushed toward a hold-up role in this pace map because the prominent slots are saturated — treat her shown position as positional context rather than a reflection of how she actually races.
runners_data.comment: April Mist won two starts back but has slipped to a seventh last time out, and our rating of 79 leaves her well below the top of this field; she has run over today's trip and going, yet that alone makes her hard to fancy from stall 8 off 126 lb.

runners_data.name: Armor Supreme
runners_data.note: The race's sole confirmed front-runner who can dictate terms entirely on his own terms under Rossa Ryan; won on this course over 5f on Good, has lightly raced form showing a peak, but the 60-day absence for Diego Dias (0/1 in 14 days) introduces a fitness query that is the one genuine threat to his lead scenario.
runners_data.comment: Armor Supreme showed smart form when winning three starts back, and her experience over today's trip and going keeps her squarely in the mix from stall 2; the main concern is that she comes here after a 60-day absence following a disappointing ninth last time out.

runners_data.name: Arrowstock
runners_data.note: Ran four times without a win or place finish on similar going for Daniel McLoughlin and was last seen just 2 days ago — brutal turnaround that raises a fatigue flag; a true prominent runner, he is displaced to midfield in this map because the field is stacked with pace types, and his STYLE_FIT of 0.93 means he needs things to go very wrong for the others.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts and returning just two days after her most recent fourth, Arrowstock faces a fitness query on a quick turnaround, though she has run over today's distance and going before and her draw of four offers a neutral pitch from which to mount a challenge.

runners_data.name: Brazilian Diva
runners_data.note: Brings a win and two places from her last six runs on Good ground and has course form over 5f; another natural prominent type for the Dias yard who could double up with Armor Supreme if she can find a clear line — jockey Diego Lima needs to navigate the crowded early order efficiently.
runners_data.comment: Brazilian Diva showed useful form when winning three starts back and a second two starts back, but has disappointed since, finishing sixth last time out; she has distance and going experience to call on and returns after 18 days, though 126 lb is no easy ask.

runners_data.name: Concorde Landed
runners_data.note: The class standout on OR 120 alongside The Baddie, with a course win over this exact 5f trip on Good going; Wayne Lordan is a major booking and Paul Twomey's yard sent out a winner recently — her only race after that debut win was a 4th, so the key question is whether that represented a blip or a ceiling.
runners_data.comment: Concorde Landed arrives with experience over today's trip and going, and her win two starts back shows the ability to compete at this level; the question is whether her fourth last time out signals she has something to find.

runners_data.name: New Bond Street
runners_data.note: The Twomey yard's second runner, ridden by Oisin Murphy; has placed three times without winning, exclusively at 6f on Good, and stepping down to 5f is unproven — though a genuine prominent type by nature, the field's pace congestion forces him wider in the map and his STYLE_FIT tag means he's unlikely to get his preferred position without a fight.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts, New Bond Street has placed twice in that run but our rating of 74 ranks her eighth of ten, making her hard to fancy despite the fitness edge of a seven-day turnaround and experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Stellar Path
runners_data.note: Wears a tongue-tie and has finished 8th or 9th in all four recent starts, including on similar going over this trip, with a flagged tendency to fade in the finish; a hold-up runner in a race that does not set up for late closers, and the OR of 57 makes it very hard to find a scenario in which she is competitive.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts, with finishes of ninth, eighth, eighth and ninth telling a grim recent story, Stellar Path is hard to fancy on these figures despite having run over today's trip and going before and the potential convenience of stall one.

runners_data.name: The Baddie
runners_data.note: A complete unknown on debut for Diego Dias — the same trainer as Armor Supreme and Brazilian Diva — with an OR of 120 implying significant home gallop evidence; running style is unclassified and the going is untested, so all assessments are speculative, but if she has genuine juvenile sprint ability the pace shape is one she could exploit from a prominent position.
runners_data.comment: Unraced and wholly unexposed, The Baddie makes her debut from stall nine carrying 126 lb, with every question still to answer but improvement guaranteed to come as she gains experience.

races.paceDynamic: Armor Supreme is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, Rossa Ryan can dictate a controlled, honest gallop from flag to finish on Good ground over this flat 5f. Behind him, a congested cluster of prominent types — Grayrobin, Star Prospect, Brazilian Diva, and Concorde Landed — will jostle for the early positions 2-3 lengths off the pace, creating compression and traffic danger between the 2f and 3f markers. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their natural position; Armor Supreme is virtually certain to lead, while Concorde Landed (OR 120, course winner) and Grayrobin are best placed to lock onto the pace end of the prominent group, with Arrowstock and New Bond Street — genuine prominent types both — likely to find themselves racing further back than ideal. With a sustainable, uncontested pace and a flat track that does not generate a strong late-closer bias on Good going, this race shape most favours horses who can sit a length or two off a controlled leader and produce a measured finish — classic prominent-to-the-front profiles win this shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Armor Supreme Controls, Prominent Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Armor Supreme dictates an uncontested, even pace and the race resolves in a tracking duel off his back.
scenarios.body: Armor Supreme sets a metronomic gallop and the winner comes from the horses able to sit closest without burning fuel in the early scramble; Concorde Landed's OR 120 and prior course win give her the class to pounce, while Grayrobin's back-to-back 5f Curragh wins make her a natural threat in this shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Holds, Leader Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent pack burns each other out in the early jostle and Armor Supreme's controlled lead proves unassailable to the line.
scenarios.body: The congestion behind Armor Supreme disrupts the rhythm of the chasers, and with Good ground and a flat track offering no late-course topography to force a challenge, the leader simply stays in front; Armor Supreme's OR 95 and course-winning form in this going make him the logical beneficiary.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Scrimmage, Midfield Capitalises
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent cluster causes significant interference 2-3f out and the race opens up for a horse who finds clear air from slightly deeper.
scenarios.body: New Bond Street or Arrowstock — both true prominent types racing further back than ideal due to field congestion — could benefit if the pace bunches dramatically and a gap materialises; their STYLE_FIT discount means this shape requires things to go exactly right, and neither has the OR to beat the top weights in a straight contest.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Sprints Through
scenarios.trigger: If The Baddie (unknown quantity, trainer Diego Dias) produces a debut performance of Concorde Landed-level class and the race unravels around her.
scenarios.body: Lightly raced debutants with an OR of 120 are rare and signal serious home expectation from the Dias yard; if she travels powerfully into the prominent group and has a sprint in reserve, the pace shape suits her perfectly, but unknown factors, debut inexperience, and the absence of form make this a low-probability outlier.

watchPoints.text: Prominent congestion between Grayrobin, Star Prospect, Brazilian Diva, and Concorde Landed is the single biggest danger point — watch for interference and bumping between the 3f and 2f poles as all four try to press Armor Supreme simultaneously.

Armor Supreme's 60-day absence is a live fitness risk — if Rossa Ryan finds the horse flat at the 1f pole after setting the pace, Concorde Landed is ideally positioned to sweep past and could win easily.

The Baddie's debut is a genuine wildcard — watch the market moves in the minutes before post time; any significant shortening from an unquoted price for the Dias yard's mystery runner should prompt a reassessment of the pace dynamic if she breaks fast and challenges Armor Supreme for the lead.

Arrowstock ran just 2 days ago and is almost certainly compromised by that brutal turnaround — watch whether Ben Coen can find any clear air from his displaced midfield position, as interference combined with fatigue makes him a significant traffic hazard for runners around him.

New Bond Street stepping from 6f down to 5f is an untested drop for Oisin Murphy — if the early pace is genuinely strong and the field strings out, watch whether he can sustain his effort in the final furlong or whether the shorter trip finds him out.

races.name: Bet With Tote On Racing & Sports Handicap

runners_data.name: Mary Shoelaces
runners_data.note: Won last time out over 5f on Good and has a strong two-wins-from-ten record on similar ground; the 7lb claimer Jessica O'Gorman keeps the weight low and the hold-up style suits a steady early pace, though 29 days since last run is no concern given the yard's decent recent return rate.
runners_data.comment: Mary Shoelaces arrives here a winner last time out and with experience of today's trip and conditions, making her a strong each-way threat from stall one; the main risk is her inconsistent recent form, with two modest efforts sandwiched around that latest success.

runners_data.name: Soulful Diva
runners_data.note: Three-year-old with a single win on Good ground over 5f; Nathan Crosse rides and the horse has shown ability when upped to this course configuration, though the wider handicap mark of 74 and a form string showing inconsistency means she needs everything to fall right from the rear.
runners_data.comment: Soulful Diva arrives with distance and going experience to call on, and her win in recent starts shows the ability is there, with our rating marking her out as the one to beat in this field; the worry is a run of four starts without troubling the judge since that victory.

runners_data.name: Arctic Steps
runners_data.note: Dylan Browne McMonagle takes the mount on this four-year-old who won over 5f Good earlier in the season; the hood (hg:p) has featured in recent starts and the horse's best form comes when getting a clear run late — 43 days off the track is the one query but the trainer has a 1/16 in the past fortnight.
runners_data.comment: Arctic Steps won three starts back but has since finished ninth and eighth in her last two, suggesting she's in a sticky patch; she has run over today's distance and going, and at 141 lb from stall 10, a return to form isn't impossible after 43 days away.

runners_data.name: Bold Optimist
runners_data.note: Ben Coen rides this consistent six-year-old who has placed four times in the last five on soft-to-good ground; the blinkers (hg:p) are worn regularly and the horse's Good-ground record of 12/15 is solid, though the Curragh 5f has only produced one win and the style demands a flawless late passage.
runners_data.comment: Bold Optimist shaped with promise when runner-up last time out, has run over today's trip and going, and our rating of 78 marks him out as a leading player from stall 2; the main concern is that he remains winless in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Harry's Hill
runners_data.note: The only confirmed prominent-style runner outside the front-runner; Paddy Harnett (5lb claim) holds the ride for Hassett and the horse has finished placed here over 5f twice recently, meaning tracking Ballysax Lil' Mick and staying on could see a honest placed effort at big odds.
runners_data.comment: Yet to score in his last six starts, Harry's Hill arrives here 29 days fresh, has run over today's trip and going, and that runner-up last time out, combined with a speed rating of 81, makes him an appealing each-way proposition from stall four carrying 139 lb.

runners_data.name: Happy Henry
runners_data.note: W McCreery's yard is in red-hot form (3/18 in 14 days) and this five-year-old has two wins and five places over 5f Good — his natural racing position is off the pace but the redistribution here means he is likely to push forward to a more prominent pitch than the map shows, which actually suits his best form where he has won tracking the pace.
runners_data.comment: Happy Henry won two starts back and has experience of today's trip and going, but he has been beaten into fifth on his most recent outing and faces a stiff task from stall 12 off 137 lb.

runners_data.name: Surpass And Shine
runners_data.note: Seamie Heffernan takes the ride on this Patrick Flynn-trained five-year-old whose one win came over 5f Good; despite being mapped to midfield, the horse's temperament means Heffernan will likely travel handier than the chart position suggests — form of 9100-0 is patchy but the Good-ground win is the relevant data point.
runners_data.comment: Surpass And Shine showed he can win when landing the spoils four starts back, but three unplaced efforts since leave him needing a return to form; he has run over today's trip and going, carries 137 lb from stall eight, and returns after 39 days off.

runners_data.name: Kiss Don't Tell
runners_data.note: Ran only two days ago which is the major flag here — that rapid turnaround for a three-year-old with an OR of 68 merits caution; the McLoughlin stable also sends out Bold Optimist so stable tactics may influence how this one is ridden, and the recent form string of 052-8 contains no Good-ground win.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts and ranked ninth of twelve on our figures, Kiss Don't Tell returns just two days after finishing eighth, and that quick turnaround makes her hard to fancy, though experience over today's trip and going counts in her favour.

runners_data.name: Heart Of Eternity
runners_data.note: Flagged as a horse that fades in the finish and carries a low OR of 56; the Denis Hogan yard is high-volume but the form string of 680000 gives no encouragement, the horse has been well beaten in seven of the last eight, and the redistribution means it will not be racing in its preferred late position — the ⚠ fade warning compounds the concern.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts and drawn from stall nine carrying 126 lb, Heart Of Eternity returns after 23 days with experience over today's trip and going in her favour, though a trainer striking at just four per cent recently offers little encouragement.

runners_data.name: Ballysax Lil' Mick
runners_data.note: The sole front-runner in the field; Wesley Joyce's 3lb claim helps at OR 48 and the horse has a clear role to play by dominating from the front — recent form over 5f on varying ground is modest (26-060) and the 53-day break is notable, but uncontested leads at this level have been the horse's only route to competitiveness.
runners_data.comment: Ballysax Lil' Mick is winless in his last five starts, with a sixth two starts back his only notable effort of late, and ranked tenth of twelve on our figures he looks up against it here; experience over today's trip and going at least removes any unknown, and 53 days off may have freshened him.

runners_data.name: Pure Valour
runners_data.note: A drop in trip from 7f-10f distances shown in the history to 5f here is a significant ask; the J G Coogan yard sends in a four-year-old whose OR of 47 reflects limited form, and although mapped to midfield through redistribution, the horse's true profile is a hold-up type who has never raced over this distance in winning form.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts and ranked bottom of this field on our figures, Pure Valour faces a stiff task, though she has experience of today's going and 46 days between runs suggests she returns fresh.

runners_data.name: Lady Landhort
runners_data.note: Flagged for fading in the finish and also ran just two days ago — a back-to-back appearance for a three-year-old at OR 48 with a Conor Cusack 7lb claimer on board; the redistribution to midfield from a true hold-up position, combined with the fade warning and rapid turnaround, makes this a very difficult proposition to assess positively.
runners_data.comment: Lady Landhort has run over today's trip and going, and a win in her last six starts offers some hope, but she returns just two days after her latest unplaced effort, ranks eleventh of twelve on our figures, and it is hard to make a strong case for her here.

races.paceDynamic: Ballysax Lil' Mick is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 12-runner 5f handicap and, with no natural rival to push them, should stride into an uncontested lead and set a controlled, honest pace on Good ground at the Curragh. Behind them, Harry's Hill is the one genuine prominent-type who is likely to slot in close to the pace, while the remainder of the field is dominated by hold-up horses — Mary Shoelaces, Soulful Diva, Arctic Steps, Bold Optimist, Happy Henry, Surpass And Shine, Heart Of Eternity, Pure Valour and Lady Landhort all prefer to come from off the pace. The field holds significantly more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate: Happy Henry, Surpass And Shine, Heart Of Eternity, Pure Valour and Lady Landhort have all been redistributed on the map, and of those, Happy Henry and Surpass And Shine are the most likely to actually push forward and secure a better position given their form profiles and competitive natures. A single front-runner dictating an unchallenged, moderate gallop on Good turf over 5f classically sets up a race for the hold-up horses who can produce a late burst — provided they get a clean run — making the late-finisher profile the primary beneficiary of this shape, with genuine hold-up horses over a trip that is quick enough to suit closers carrying big handicap weights.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Ballysax Lil' Mick dictates an uncontested, confidence-sapping tempo that softens the late challenge.
scenarios.body: Lil' Mick bowls along unchallenged from the front, sets a comfortable pace that never truly tests the closers, and the prominent Harry's Hill tracks close enough to grab second; on Good turf over 5f a solo front-runner who is never headed can steal an unassailable break at the two-furlong pole.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Land Late
scenarios.trigger: If the honest but moderate pace set by Ballysax Lil' Mick is sufficient to tow the hold-up horses into range at the furlong pole.
scenarios.body: The true hold-up horses — Mary Shoelaces, Soulful Diva and Arctic Steps — get a clean passage through and produce their best late effort; on this track at 5f, genuine closers with recent Good-ground wins have the form profile to arrive at the right moment if the pace is steady enough to keep them covered.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Movers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the redistributed prominent types — Happy Henry and Surpass And Shine — successfully push forward early and turn this into a tactical dash for the wire.
scenarios.body: Happy Henry, with a superior sim-going strike rate and multiple wins on Good turf, pushes to a handy position and proves too sharp for true hold-up horses coming from further back; Surpass And Shine, having won off similar ground, could also land a blow if allowed to travel comfortably in a prominent position rather than being bottled up in the rear.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Race Collapses For Closers
scenarios.trigger: If the pace completely falls away in the final furlong and a mad scramble develops, negating any advantage the front-runner has built.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires Ballysax Lil' Mick to capitulate sharply and the closers to all arrive in a bunched finish; Bold Optimist and Arctic Steps, who carry headgear and have placed form on Good ground, would be the most likely beneficiaries of late carnage, though the probability is low given a solo front-runner who is unlikely to be pressured into unsustainable fractions.

watchPoints.text: Ballysax Lil' Mick breaks cleanly — if Wesley Joyce establishes a clear lead unchallenged inside the first furlong, this horse's entire chance rests on front-running, so any stumble or slow break eliminates the scenario entirely.

Happy Henry's early position is critical — if Leigh Roche allows the horse to drift back into a genuine hold-up position rather than pushing forward, the McCreery yard's form advantage is wasted; watch for him to be sent forward at the start.

Kiss Don't Tell and Lady Landhort both ran just 48 hours ago — if either shows signs of distress or is pulled up, the McLoughlin stable's three-runner strategy collapses and Bold Optimist becomes the yard's sole live hope.

Surpass And Shine's draw and early foot will determine whether Seamie Heffernan can get the horse into a handier position than its natural hold-up style dictates — a wide draw or slow start pins it to the back and sharply reduces its winning chance.

The going report consistently shows Good for both 5f races today (4:55 and 5:25), confirming no material surface deterioration — horses with Good-ground form can be taken at face value and no going bias adjustment is required for this race.
